distances.verdict: TIGHT: every run needs 9.5 s more lead time than the clearance interval allows. EMS delay difference 0.47 s is inside the noise floor (95% CI [-13.96, 20.6] includes zero), so this point does not establish a winner.
OK: every run is planned with lead time to spare. EMS delay difference -14.1 s is inside the noise floor (95% CI [-44.52, 25.64] includes zero), so this point does not establish a winner.

modelNote: The emergency vehicle is spawned at its physical detection distance through SimEngine.spawnEmsAt, and the approach is lengthened to distance + 60 m so the vehicle fits. Lengthening the approach also adds storage; background demand is identical across points and laneLengthM is reported per row so that confound is auditable. Delay is measured from the emsMilestone/boxExited event; seeds with no observed exit are counted in unobservedSeeds and excluded from the mean rather than replaced with a placeholder.
narrative: Detection at 150 m produced TIGHT plans. Yellow (3.5 s) and all-red (2.0 s) are fixed by Safety Kernel invariants I2 and I5, so the only recourse is to accept the shortfall and record it; the controller may not shorten clearance to buy the missing seconds. Longer detection distances produce OK plans because the ETA covers the full required lead time.
